Rashi on Chullin 74b:10:2.hebrew: בבן פקועה - בשה בן ט' חי הנמצא בבהמה שנשחטה; ובפחות משווייו קמיבעיא ליה, דאי בשווייו, קיימא לן בבכורות (דף יא.) דאפילו בשלקי מפרקינן:
Rashi on Chullin 74b:10:2.english: With a ben pekua - [i.e.,] with a live nine-[month-old] lamb found inside an animal that was slaughtered; and it is regarding [a lamb worth] less than its [the donkey's] value that the dilemma is raised, for if [it is worth] its [full] value, it is established for us in Bekhorot (11a) that we may even redeem [a firstborn donkey] with cooked food:

Rashi on Chullin 74b:11:1.hebrew: כבשרא בדיקולא הוא - ותנן בבכורות (דף יב.): אין פודין בשחוטה:
Rashi on Chullin 74b:11:1.english: It is like meat in a basket - And we learned in a Mishnah in Bekhorot (12a): One may not redeem [a firstborn donkey] with a slaughtered [animal]:

Rashi on Chullin 74b:13:1.hebrew: דגמר שה שה מפסחים - ופסח בבן פקועה פסול, דקיימא לן (לעיל חולין דף לח:) בקדשים: "כי יולד" — פרט ליוצא דופן:
Rashi on Chullin 74b:13:1.english: Because he derives “lamb,” “lamb” from Paschal offerings - And a Paschal offering [brought] from a ben pekua is invalid, as we hold (above, Chullin 38b) regarding consecrated offerings: “When it is born” — [this] excludes an animal delivered by Caesarean section:

Rashi on Chullin 74b:15:1.english: All things - Such as a ben pekua:

Rashi on Chullin 74b:15:2.hebrew: מאי אהני ליה - ומסתברא דהאי ממעט, דכבישרא בדיקולא הוא, וכי מרבי, בעל מום ונקבה קא מרבי:
Rashi on Chullin 74b:15:2.english: What purpose does it serve - And it stands to reason that this [verbal analogy] excludes [a ben pekua], since it is like meat in a basket, and when [the verse] amplifies, it amplifies a blemished [animal] and a female:

Rashi on Chullin 74b:16:1.hebrew: איבעיא להו - נטמאה בהמה שחוטה, מהו למנותה ראשון ובן ט' חי שבבטנה שני:
Rashi on Chullin 74b:16:1.english: A dilemma was raised before them - [If] a slaughtered animal became ritually impure, what is [the law with regard to] counting it [as having] first-[degree impurity] and a living nine-[month fetus] in its belly [as having] second-[degree impurity]?

Rashi on Chullin 74b:17:1.english: One counts - because they are two [separate] bodies:

Rashi on Chullin 74b:17:2.hebrew: אין מונין - אלא איהו נמי הוי ראשון, דנעשה כאגוז המתקשקש בקליפתו, שהבהמה שומר שלו:
Rashi on Chullin 74b:17:2.english: One does not count - Rather, it [the fetus] is also first-[degree impure], for it is considered like a nut rattling in its shell, as the [mother] animal is its protector:

Rashi on Chullin 74b:18:1.english: The flesh [is rendered impure through] contact with a carcass - [This refers to] the flesh of the fetus that was attached to the limb that extended [outside the womb]:

Rashi on Chullin 74b:1:1.hebrew: ר"ש שזורי - בגמרא פריך: היינו תנא קמא:
Rashi on Chullin 74b:1:1.english: Rabbi Shimon Shezuri - In the Gemara it asks: [Isn't] this [the same as] the first Tanna [Tanna Kamma]?

Rashi on Chullin 74b:1:2.english: He tore it - the animal, without slaughter:

Rashi on Chullin 74b:20:1.hebrew: בדמא דאמיה - דכיון שהוכשר בית השחיטה בדם, הוכשרה וכו':
Rashi on Chullin 74b:20:1.english: Through the blood of its mother - For once the site of slaughter was rendered susceptible [to ritual impurity] by the blood, [the mother] was rendered susceptible, etc.:

Rashi on Chullin 74b:20:2.english: Through what is it rendered susceptible - [i.e.,] the flesh of the fetus, so that it may contract impurity from [the] limb:

Rashi on Chullin 74b:21:1.hebrew: בשחיטה - כיון שהוא ניתר בשחיטה, הוכשר בה לטומאה; וכר"ש, דאמר שחיטה מכשרת ולא דם, בפ"ב (לעיל חולין דף לג.):
Rashi on Chullin 74b:21:1.english: Through the slaughter - Since it [the fetus] is permitted [for consumption] through the slaughter [of its mother], it is rendered susceptible to ritual impurity through it; and [this is in accordance with] Rabbi Shimon, who says that slaughter renders [meat] susceptible [to impurity], and not blood, in the second chapter (above, Chullin 33a):

Rashi on Chullin 74b:22:1.hebrew: עבר בנהר - בן ט' חי שנמצא בשחוטה וגדל:
Rashi on Chullin 74b:22:1.english: Passed through a river - [This refers to] a live nine-[month fetus] that was found in a slaughtered [animal] and grew up:

Rashi on Chullin 74b:2:1.english: They did not proceed with it - with this fetus, to be lenient:

Rashi on Chullin 74b:2:2.hebrew: אלא על עסקי שחיטה בלבד - אבל לשאר דבריו, מודו רבנן דבהמה מעלייתא היא:
Rashi on Chullin 74b:2:2.english: Only with regard to the matter of slaughter - But with respect to its other matters, the Rabbis agree that it is a full-fledged animal:

Rashi on Chullin 74b:2:3.hebrew: למעוטי חלבו וגידו - דכיון דמצאוהו חי, חדשים ואוירא גרמי לאסור חלבו וגידו:
Rashi on Chullin 74b:2:3.english: To exclude its fat and its [sciatic] nerve - Since they found it alive, [its completed] months [of gestation] and the air [it breathed] cause its fat and its [sciatic] nerve to be forbidden:

Rashi on Chullin 74b:3:1.hebrew: חלבו דמאי - אע"פ שהוא בכל הספרים, אמת הדבר שהוא שבוש, ולא יש חכם אשר יושיבנו על כנו, דהיכי בעי "חלבו דמאי"? והא ודאי ליכא לאוקומי מילתיה אלא אשליל דבן ט' חי, דהא עליה קאי. אלא בפרק דגיד הנשה גרסינן לה לכולה כי הא, ואגב שיטפא דגירסא אישתבשו בה למיגרס' הכא. והכי גרסינן: "והא מיפלג פליגי דתניא כו' וא"ר אלעזר א"ר אושעיא מחלוקת כו'" עד "ור' יהודה לשיטתו, אלא אי אתמר כו'", ולא גרסינן בהאי פירקא אלא "חלבו דגיד", אבל בפ' גיד הנשה גרסינן לה. והכי פירושו: "והא מיפלג פליגי" — בין בחלב בין בגיד — "דתניא: גיד הנשה נוהג בשליל וחלבו של שליל אסור", וכדמפרש בבן ט' חי, דקסבר חדשים ואוירא גרמי, ואע"פ שנשחטה אמו והוציאוהו:
Rashi on Chullin 74b:3:1.english: Whose fat - Although this [phrase] appears in all the books, the truth of the matter is that it is a textual error, and there is no scholar who can set it right. For how could [the Gemara] ask, "Whose fat?" Surely one cannot establish its statement except regarding a live nine-month-old fetus, for it is referring to that. Rather, in the chapter of Gid HaNasheh, we read this entire [passage] in this form, and due to the flow of the text they erred by reading it here [as well]. Thus we should read: "But do they not disagree, as it is taught, etc., and Rabbi Elazar said in the name of Rabbi Oshaya: The dispute, etc." until "and Rabbi Yehuda follows his reasoning; rather, if it was stated, etc." And we do not read in this chapter anything except "the fat of the gid," whereas in the chapter of Gid HaNasheh we read it [in full]. And this is its explanation: "But do they not disagree" — both regarding the fat and regarding the gid [sciatic nerve] — "as it is taught [in a baraita]: The sciatic nerve applies to a fetus, and the fat of the fetus is forbidden," and as [the Gemara] explains, "regarding a live nine-month-old [fetus]," for he holds that [gestational] months and [exposure to] air cause [it to be considered an independent animal], even though its mother was slaughtered and they took it out:

Rashi on Chullin 74b:3:2.hebrew: והלך ר"מ לשיטתו - דמשוי ליה בהמה לענין שחיטה:
Rashi on Chullin 74b:3:2.english: And Rabbi Meir follows his [own] reasoning - for he treats it as an animal with regard to slaughter:

Rashi on Chullin 74b:4:1.english: From its root - even [that which is] absorbed and rooted in its flesh:

Rashi on Chullin 74b:4:2.hebrew: גוממו עם השופי - כלומר, חותכו בשוה לשופי, ונוטל את הגבוה מן השופי דדמי לגיד ואסור מדרבנן, אבל שרשין של חלבו מותרין:
Rashi on Chullin 74b:4:2.english: He trims it level with the smooth surface [of the flesh] - That is to say, he cuts it even with the smooth surface [of the flesh], and removes [the fat] that rises above the smooth surface, as it resembles the [sciatic] nerve and is prohibited by rabbinic law; however, the roots of its fat [sunk inside the flesh] are permitted:

Rashi on Chullin 74b:5:1.english: They did not proceed regarding it - [That is,] the Sages [did not rule] regarding the fetus with this permit that does not treat it as an animal:

Rashi on Chullin 74b:5:2.english: Only with regard to matters of consumption - to eat it without slaughter, and to eat its [forbidden] fat and its [sciatic] nerve:

Rashi on Chullin 74b:5:3.hebrew: למעוטי רובעו וחורש בו - בכלאים, בשור וחמור, דודאי לוקה:
Rashi on Chullin 74b:5:3.english: To exclude one who copulates with it or plows with it - [i.e., plowing] with diverse kinds, [such as] with an ox and a donkey, for he certainly incurs lashes:

Rashi on Chullin 74b:7:1.hebrew: קורעו ומוציא את דמו - אלמא אפילו בן ח', דלכולי עלמא חלבו מותר, קתני מתני' קורעו:
Rashi on Chullin 74b:7:1.english: One tears it and removes its blood - Thus, even [in the case of] an eight-[month-old fetus], whose fat is permitted according to all [opinions], the Mishnah teaches, "one tears it [and removes its blood]."

Rashi on Chullin 74b:7:2.hebrew: לומר שאין ענוש כרת - האי "מתיר בדמו" דקאמר ריש לקיש, לאו היתר לכתחלה:
Rashi on Chullin 74b:7:2.english: To say that one is not punished with karet - This [statement], "he permits its blood," that [Reish Lakish] said is not an ab initio permission:

Rashi on Chullin 74b:8:1.english: According to whom do we say [this] - who is the one who permits its fat:

Rashi on Chullin 74b:8:2.hebrew: לרבי יהודה - כדקתני לעיל "וחלבו מותר", ולר' יהודה אמאי אין ענוש כרת על דמו? דלא גרע מדם התמצית, דלאו דם הנפש הוא, וקמחייב עליה ר' יהודה כרת:
Rashi on Chullin 74b:8:2.english: According to Rabbi Yehuda - as it was taught above, "and its fat is permitted." Yet according to Rabbi Yehuda, why is one not punished with karet for [consuming] its blood? For it is no less [stringent] than blood of exudate, which is not blood of the soul, and [yet] Rabbi Yehuda holds one liable to karet for it:

Rashi on Chullin 74b:8:3.hebrew: באזהרה - בפ"ק דכריתות מפרש: ה' לאוין כתיבי בדם:
Rashi on Chullin 74b:8:3.english: By a prohibition - In the first chapter of Keritot, [the Gemara] explains: five prohibitions are written regarding blood:

Rashi on Chullin 74b:8:4.english: By karet - for he derives it from the inclusive expression "any blood":

Rashi on Chullin 74b:9:1.hebrew: אית ליה לר' יהודה דם וכל דם - כלומר, כיון דר' יהודה לדם התמצית מריבוי' ד"כל דם" יליף, אקושי מקיש "כל דם" ל"דם" עצמו:
Rashi on Chullin 74b:9:1.english: Rabbi Yehuda holds [the exposition of] "blood" and "any blood" - That is to say, since Rabbi Yehuda derives [the prohibition of] blood of exudate from the amplification [implied by] "any blood," he equates "any blood" to "blood" itself:

Rashi on Chullin 74b:9:2.hebrew: כל היכא דמיחייב אדם - מחייב אכל דם, והיכא דלא מחייב אעיקר דם, כגון שליל שאין בו דם הנפש, לא מחייב על דם איבריו:
Rashi on Chullin 74b:9:2.english: Wherever one is liable for blood [of the soul] - he is [also] liable for any blood, and wherever he is not liable for the primary blood, such as [that of] a fetus, which does not have blood of the soul, he is not liable for the blood of its limbs:

Tosafot on Chullin 74b:13:1.hebrew: דגמר שה שה מפסח - פירש בקונטרס דפסח פסול משום יוצא דופן, ואי אפשר לומר כן, דא"כ לר"מ היאך פודין בו, דאמר לעיל דאליבא דר"מ שה מעליא הוא ופודין בו? אלא מיפסיל מטעם שחוטה, דאין פודין בשחוטה, כדאמר בפ"ק דבכורות (דף יב.):
Tosafot on Chullin 74b:13:1.english: Because you derive "lamb" "lamb" from a Paschal offering - Rashi explained that a Paschal offering is disqualified on account of [being like] an animal delivered by Caesarean section [yotzei dofen]. But it is impossible to say this, for if so, according to Rabbi Meir, how can one redeem [a firstborn donkey] with it, given that [the Gemara] stated above that according to Rabbi Meir it is a proper lamb and one may redeem with it? Rather, it is disqualified on account of [being considered] a slaughtered animal, for one does not redeem with a slaughtered animal, as [the Gemara] states in the first chapter of Bekhorot (12a):

Tosafot on Chullin 74b:3:1.hebrew: חלבו דמאי - בקונטרס לא גריס ליה, דפשיטא דבשליל איירי, ולא גרסינן "אלא חלבו דגיד", דלא איירי בבהמה אלא בשליל. ור"ת אומר שיש ליישב הגירסא, וה"פ: חלבו דמאי? אילימא חלבו דשליל — כלומר, דגוף דשליל, כגון חלב הכליות ושעל הקרב, ואתא לאפוקי מחלב דגיד דשליל — והא מיפלג פליגי, דשרי ר' יהודה חלבו וגיד דשליל של בן ט'! אלא חלבו דגיד, דלא פליג ר"מ אלא לענין שחיטה, אבל חלבו דגידו שרי — והא דקאמר לעיל "למעוטי חלבו וגידו", כלומר היינו חלבו דגידו, אי נמי, "וגידו" נקט לקנוקנות, דשרי — הא פליג ר"מ ואסר אפי' חלב דגיד וקנוקנות דשליל, מדקתני "כל מקום שהוא", משמע אפילו דשליל, וקתני "חותך שומנו מעיקרו וגם מחטט אחריו", משמע דאסר אפילו קנוקנות. וכי קאמר "חלבו דגיד", הוה מצי למיפרך: מ"מ, אמאי נקט רבי אושעיא "אלא על עסקי שחיטה בלבד", כיון דפליג נמי בחלב כליות ודקרב ודגיד דשליל? אלא דעדיפא פריך, דבחלב גיד נמי פליגי. ומהאי טעמא נמי לא קאמר "למעוטי דמו", דהוי לכ"ע בכרת, משום ד"אלא על עסקי שחיטה" קאמר, ואכתי תקשה לן: הא פליגי נמי בחלבו וגידו! ולכך הוצרך לומר ד"אלא על עסקי אכילה בלבד" אתמר, והא דפליגי באותו ואת בנו, בכלל אכילה הוא:
Tosafot on Chullin 74b:3:1.english: The fat of which [part] - In Rashi, he does not have this reading, for it is obvious that [the Gemara] is dealing with a fetus; and [according to him] we do not read "Rather, the fat of the nerve," since it is not dealing with an [adult] animal, only with a fetus. And Rabbeinu Tam says that the [printed] reading can be reconciled, and this is its explanation: "The fat of which [part]? If we say the fat of the fetus" — that is to say, of the body of the fetus, such as the fat of the kidneys and [that] which is on the innards, and [the Gemara] is coming to exclude the fat of the nerve of the fetus — "why, they disagree," for Rabbi Yehuda permits the fat and the nerve of a nine-[month-old] fetus! Rather, [it means] "the fat of the nerve," for Rabbi Meir only disagrees regarding the matter of slaughter, whereas the fat of its nerve is permitted — and that which [the Gemara] says above, "to exclude its fat and its nerve," that is to say, this means the fat of its nerve; alternatively, it mentioned "and its nerve" for the branching sinews, which are permitted — [to which the Gemara objects:] Why, Rabbi Meir disagrees and prohibits even the fat of the nerve and the branching sinews of a fetus! From [the fact] that [the baraita] teaches "in any place that it is," it implies even [that] of a fetus; and it teaches "one cuts out its fat from its root and also scrapes around it," which implies that he prohibits even the branching sinews. And when [the Gemara] says "the fat of the nerve," it could have asked: In any case, why did Rabbi Oshaya state "only with regard to the matter of slaughter," since [Rabbi Yehuda] also disagrees regarding the fat of the kidneys, and of the innards, and of the nerve of a fetus? Rather, it asks a stronger [objection], that they disagree regarding the fat of the nerve as well. And for this reason as well, [the Gemara] does not say "to exclude its blood," which according to everyone incurs karet, because [Rabbi Oshaya] said "only with regard to the matter of slaughter," and it would still be difficult for us: why, they also disagree regarding its fat and its nerve! Therefore, [the Gemara] had to say that it was stated "only with regard to the matter of eating"; and that which they disagree regarding [the prohibition of] "it and its young" is included under eating:

Tosafot on Chullin 74b:5:1.hebrew: למעוטי רובעו - דס"ד דגרע מבהמה מפרכסת דחייב רובע, כדאמרינן בפ' העור והרוטב (לקמן חולין דף קכא:). אי נמי, התם הני מילי כגון ישראל בטמאה ועובד כוכבי' בטהורה, אבל הכא, דבשחיטה זו משתריא באכילה, סלקא דעתך לא מחייב:
Tosafot on Chullin 74b:5:1.english: To exclude one who copulates with it - For it would have entered your mind [to say] that [the fetus] is inferior to a convulsing animal, regarding which one who copulates with it is liable, as we say in the chapter [entitled] HaOr VeHaRotev (below, Chullin 121b). Alternatively, there, this applies only [in a case] such as a Jew with a non-kosher animal or an idolater with a kosher animal; but here, where through this slaughter it is permitted for consumption, it would have entered your mind [that] he is not liable:
